value.account:
CHANGED. New modules: workflow/resume_loop_progress.py (for_each / repeat_until progress validation, ResumeProjectionValidationError), workflow/resume_slots.py (slot index, exact id and call-boundary resolution, re-exported through WorkflowStateProjection.enumerate_resume_slots / resolve_resume_step_id / resolve_call_boundary), workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py (index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id), workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (ResumeScopePath, audit_scope, audit_call_frames, the v1 diagnostic), loader_imports.py (duplicate import alias / section scan on the composed YAML node graph), observability/forensic.py. Wiring: CallBoundaryProjection.import_alias and a projection-level repeat_until_max_iterations map; StateManager.record_workflow_checksum_mismatch / record_resume_projection_integrity_failure (raw-JSON read-modify-write of status/error/updated_at only, so unknown root fields survive); the CLI now loads the bundle, keeps the root checksum precheck, then calls the module-level audit_scope before observability overrides, session/process metadata and executor construction, and a failing session close is logged instead of replacing the diagnostic; WorkflowExecutor.execute rechecks the checksum via calculate_checksum and audits the root before the prologue unless the state manager is a call-frame manager; CallExecutor selects the frame through the lineage (running member, else next retry ordinal), rejects a completed frame on the occupied id with completed_call_frame_id_collision, and after the input/write-root/checksum/bound-input validation resolves the one current boundary (one projection.resolve_call_boundary call), selects the callee by the boundary alias, validates failed predecessors then the running member through calls.audit_scope, and only then builds the frame manager and child executor; a child projection error is returned unwrapped instead of call_failed. Sticky failure: _handle_control_flow returns _stop and records the run error before any goto/on_error handling (also for for_each result lists), repeat_until no longer wraps it, for_each / typed loop bodies stop, and FinalizationController records an ordinary cleanup failure as failure.error=None under a projection error without replacing it. Workflow Lisp provenance is now set where the compiler lowers (elaborate_surface_workflow(frontend_kind=...)) and build_frontend_bundle no longer overwrites it; _is_workflow_lisp_target reads only provenance.frontend_kind. Status snapshot, monitor classifier/messages and the dashboard cursor treat the current_step left by either envelope as forensic. specs/state.md has the new section and specs/acceptance/index.md items 201-208.

TESTS. New: test_resume_projection_integrity.py (reasons, exact loop messages, slots, lineage, source-scan of the auditor), test_resume_projection_integrity_runtime.py (envelope deltas, ordering, second root audit with session metadata, sticky routes / on_error / for_each / repeat_until, cleanup supplemental failure, collision, Workflow Lisp lineage order, loop-contained calls, forensic status), test_workflow_import_alias_duplicates.py, test_workflow_lisp_frontend_provenance.py. The full suite has the same 47 failures as an unmodified `git archive` copy of HEAD (checked with a baseline run), and no new ones. I mutated the sticky and loop-stop code to confirm those tests fail without it.

EXISTING TESTS I HAD TO CHANGE (contract changes, not weakened checks): the characterization tests that froze the old gaps (stale caller starting a fresh child, callee-local corruption mutating parent and child, malformed call_frames reaching execute_call, CLI/direct-executor mutation order, current_step name mismatch now reported as presentation_slot_mismatch) now assert the new fail-closed behaviour; hand-seeded current_step rows gained the mandatory step_id; two Workflow Lisp fixtures no longer pop only the loop frame row while keeping exhausted bookkeeping; three fake-bundle CLI tests patch audit_scope; direct-compile Workflow Lisp tests that resume now pass a step-granular (lowering schema 1) run context because the bundles became typed workflow_lisp; one lexical-restore test that deliberately builds an inconsistent loop state patches executor.audit_scope; the adjudication sidecar-mismatch test patches _root_checksum_mismatch because it edits the workflow on purpose; two wcc golden files gained call-boundary import_alias.

ALTERNATIVES. (1) I first put max_iterations on IterationStepKeyProjection; the structural goldens serialize that dataclass and diverged, and the spec does not list the field, so I moved it to a separate WorkflowStateProjection map. (2) Auditing the whole child-frame tree from the root audit was rejected: the spec audits each scope when it is reached, and the callee bundle is only known then. (3) Using the patched `resolve_call_boundary` projection method inside the frame-table audit was rejected so a test counting calls sees exactly one per reached call identity (the auditor uses the module function). (4) Failing the CLI on a non-bundle object was avoided by patching audit_scope in the tests rather than adding isinstance guards to production code.

NOT COVERED / JUDGEMENT CALLS. repeat_until ordering of the four forms uses my reading of the spec: an active iteration may carry a condition result for the current iteration (an existing test seeds that), and a terminal failed exhaustion without a persisted loop frame row is rejected. Unspecified messages I added: `for_each.<n>.current_index is out of range`, `.completed_indices must be a list`, and an unknown loop name in for_each/repeat_until bookkeeping is invalid_loop_progress. List-shaped for_each result rows (steps.<loop> as a list) are not audited for their nested step ids; only the flat `Loop[i].Step` rows are. Deeper nested-loop iteration rows are not enumerated. expected_owner.workflow_file for a child scope is derived by matching the frame state's recorded workflow_file against the bundle path (no workspace is available to the auditor). A run already `completed` is not audited by the CLI. Dashboard and monitor forensic handling is covered by the status snapshot test only. I did not write a docs/plans entry, did not commit, and the Workflow Lisp lineage tests type a classic bundle via provenance replacement rather than compiling a real .orc retry scenario.
value.summary: Resume now audits every persisted identity against the current projection (CLI root, structural-root executor, each reached call and retry lineage) and fails closed with one sticky, non-routable `resume_projection_integrity_error` before any mutation or effect, with the envelopes, loader alias checks, typed Workflow Lisp provenance, forensic status handling, specs and tests in place.
